meta.title: lpdf Showcase — Capping Text
meta.subject: max-lines and ellipsis on a text of the layout

column.text: max-lines keeps a text to a number of lines, and ellipsis marks what it dropped.
One long name or address makes its whole row tall.

column.text: With a cap and an ellipsis
The product keeps one line and the address two, each ending in dots where text was dropped.

column.text: max-lines="2" alone: the text stops at the end of its second line.
A description that runs on: it says what the product is, what it is made of, how it ships and how long the warranty lasts, which takes more than two lines at this width.
ellipsis="true" alone changes nothing: the text wraps whole, and a word wider than its box is drawn whole.
Shipping is free on orders over fifty dollars. Electroencephalographically
A capped text across a page break
This box fills the page so that the text after it starts with room for three lines. The text has max-lines="6" and ellipsis="true", and is long enough for many more lines.

The capped text starts here, near the bottom of the page. It is a long paragraph, the kind a terms and conditions block or a notes field holds, and it would fill much of the next page if nothing capped it. With max-lines it keeps its first six lines and drops the rest. The page break falls inside those six lines, so three of them stay on this page and three go to the next, and the last line kept ends in dots. Nothing past that line is drawn, on the next page or on any page after it, however much text there is. The words from here on only make the text long. A payment is due thirty days after the date of the invoice. Goods remain the property of the seller until they are paid for in full. Returns are accepted within fourteen days of delivery, in the original packaging and with the receipt. A restocking fee may apply to items that were opened. Claims for damage in transit must be made within forty-eight hours of delivery, with photographs of the package and of the item. The seller is not liable for delays caused by the carrier, by customs or by events outside its control. These terms are governed by the law of the place where the seller is registered.
This line follows the capped text on the next page.
